comparator.name: Rechtsgeleerdheid
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum accounts for 180 EC as three 60-EC years. Year one contains ten 6-EC components spanning legal foundations, criminal law, private law, constitutional and administrative law, rule of law and democracy, international and European law, law and behaviour, legal professions and ethics, persons and family law, and a digitalisation project. The Amsterdam Law Firm 1.1 and 1.2 skills sessions carry no separately stated EC and are not added to the 180-EC reconstruction. Year two contains ten 6-EC components: European Law, property law, legal history, obligations, the Damage and Law project, administrative law, substantive criminal law, administrative procedural law, formal criminal law, and the Sustainability project; Amsterdam Law Firm 2.1 and 2.2 likewise carry no separately stated EC. Year three contains international public law (6), legal philosophy (6), Law and Practice (3), genuine free-choice space (15), civil procedure (6), corporate law (6), one 6-EC integration choice, Fundamental Rights (6), and the bachelor thesis (6). The integration choice is instantiated as Insolvency Law because it is the first official-listed option; Labour Law is an equally valid alternative and this restricted choice is not a formal route. The page says its information applies to the current study year and may change for the next year, so it is not treated as a guaranteed fixed entrant-cohort schedule.

components.name: Integratievak Insolventierecht
components.note: One of two restricted integration choices; the first official-listed option is selected as the neutral tie-break.

components.name: Bachelorscriptie
components.note: Compulsory independent legal research and writing capstone.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal and private law, political philosophy, ethics, persuasive communication and negotiation. Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising emphasis shifts to public institutions, cross-border orders and their historical and social contexts.
